title: Work IQ: agents can execute reusable recipes
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and general Work IQ controls are supported, and it appropriately leaves recipe-specific behaviour and licensing unconfirmed. Two Graph calls need minor formatting corrections: move their request-body properties into notes.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals with appId fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 provisions the Work IQ resource.
claims.quote: Set the method to POST and the URL to https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals. ... "appId": "fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7"
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api.call and its rendered call to 'POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals'. Add the note 'The request body sets appId to fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7.' Keep the existing documentation link.

claims.claim: App consent is granted in Microsoft Entra admin center at Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions > Grant admin consent for [your tenant].
claims.quote: Grant consent: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Entra ID > App registrations > select the app > API permissions. Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant].

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants can grant WorkIQAgent.Ask for all users using clientId, consentType AllPrincipals, resourceId and scope.
claims.quote: The consentType is AllPrincipals, indicating that you're consenting on behalf of all users in the tenant. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and its rendered call to 'POST /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants'. Add to its note: 'The request body sets clientId to the client service principal object ID, consentType to AllPrincipals, resourceId to the Work IQ service principal object ID, and scope to WorkIQAgent.Ask. Revoke with DELETE /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants/{grant-id}.' The existing Graph link documents both operations; the cited Create oAuth2PermissionGrant reference confirms all four properties.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy documentation says mutation operations are not allowed by default for safety.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported Work IQ MCP mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.
